text:
Veggie Lovers absolutely knocks all of the other vegetarian Chinese places out of the water. Every one of them. New Harmony, suck it. Kingdom of Vegetarians, your food is not good. 

The food at Veggie Lovers is fresh, all prepared to order. They emphasize in the menu preface that nothing is frozen, from a can, or pre-made, and the care they take in preparing it really shows. The food is flavorful, light, and absent of the sickeningly sweet, greasy, heavy sauces of most Chinese food. Not to fret, though - the menu includes all of the Chinese takeout favorites and then some. 

I've had a variety of dishes at Veggie Lovers, but favorites include hot and sour soup (could be spicier, easily fixed with the chili oil sitting at every table), sesame chicken (the broccoli is actually crispy!), kale with bean curd (order it light on the salt), Singapore-style noodles, and spring rolls. 

Yes, the menu is entirely vegetarian, but even for meat-eaters, the food is leagues above your typical takeout. In fact, on a recent dining experience, I learned that Veggie Lovers has been ranked in the top 100 Chinese dining establishments in the country (out of some 41,000) by the Chinese Restaurant Foundation. 

Food aside, the ambiance is great. The place is clean, nicely decorated, and has a very home-y feel. The owners, a husband and wife team, are incredibly nice (as are their two kids), and the service is quick.

My girlfriend and I have been coming here for about a year, and we cannot fathom eating at any other Chinese restaurant ever again.

One thing is for sure. I will definitely return! Everything from the food, wine, & service, to the ambiance was excellent. The two specials were salmon and tilapia. My friend had the tilapia, & I had the salmon. We paired it with our favorite Pinot Noir, & it was delicious! The salmon with a béarnaise sauce, I think literally melted in my mouth & disappeared off my plate! Yum.

Our servers created a wonderfully attentive, yet relaxed atmosphere from start to finish. This was indeed, exactly the goal of an evening between besties in need of some downtime to catch up over wine & food. A most enjoyable girl's night = success:D

The Corn Cheese dish is divine. I would come here and just eat that. This place is pretty decent for Korean bbq but it's not all-you-can eat and it's quite pricey. We got the garlic pork belly and the Gal Bi and I've definitely had better at other kbbq places in Nola. The marinade was a bit off. But the appetizers here are definitely A+. Highly recommend the Honey bbq chicken and the corn cheese. 

Overall, good experience for Korean bbq, great staff, and a great ambiance.

Great experience and food was amazing during our recent lunch visit. Started with papadum and the homemade chutneys were so good. I had the Santa Barbara Uni Biryani absolutely delicious! My son husband had the Thali and the butter chicken and the beef korma both delicious! Ended the lunch with the cardamom and pistachio ice cream that was served in a metal syringe looking thing and absolutely tasty! Wait staff could be more confident and engaging but definitely not a put off. Small plates don't expect massive amounts of food - it was just right. Presentation of food was great. Food memorable and yummy. Looking forward to going back for dinner.

Obviously, you come to a chophouse for steaks. Turns out, they don't know how to cook a steak. I guess their signature style is to be charred on both sides, but our steaks were so charred they were straight up burnt. It was almost hard to eat, and I eventually cut off the top and bottom. The only good thing I can say about it was that it was a quality cut of meat and was cooked medium rare to perfection inside.
What you need to order when you come here is the New York Style Thick Cut Sizzling Bacon and the baked shrimp. We had both for appetizers, and I would go there again just to order those 2 things. 
The ambience was great: it was dimly lit and pretty quiet. A pianist came out around 6 pm. The service was also very good. Our waitress was very friendly and answered all of our questions. Plus, she kept my tea refilled, which is a hard task!

I needed somewhere to eat before a production of one of my plays, and as per my fellow Yelpers, this seemed to balance proximity with quality, so off I went. The GPS directions that came from Yelp were off, and apparently put me on the other side of the street (which I only figured out after completely missing the restaurant and eventually turning around and finding it), but that's on Yelp or my GPS.

In any case, it's a cute little spot in a strip mall, and while it's not fancy, the inside is actually rather pleasant and welcoming, with shining black tables and brick. Service is super friendly and attentive; I felt very welcome from the moment I set foot inside, and they were great about keeping the water glass full and wiping my place (and I wasn't particularly messy) after each course.

The food is something of a hybrid. There is a page of traditional Vietnamese items, but there are also a few Thai dishes and then some dishes that are largely French. I opted for a pair of specials, both of which were more French. I liked how the server gave the price of each special as he described it, though admittedly he slipped up in not telling me the specials before I asked if there were any. I think he didn't realize I hadn't been told them, because with the next table, I heard him ask if someone had told them the specials yet.

My starter was a mushroom puree soup. It wouldn't have won a beauty pageant--mushrooms aren't exactly gorgeous in puree form--but it was indeed very tasty, and it wasn't so completely pureed that it had no texture.

My main course was a roast duck with strawberry chutney, which came accompanied by broccoli and potato (almost like a little lasagna stack of slices). This course was a mixed bag. On the plus side, the duck was tender and other than a bit of the breast, pretty moist. Much of the skin was really crisp and delicious. The potato "lasagna" (my name) was quite tasty, and the broccoli was nicely cooked. Having said all that, not all of the skin was crispy, and there were places where the fat wasn't rendered and just had to be cut away. That wasn't a big deal, though. The dish's biggest weakness was the strawberry chutney: the sauce was so thin and watery that it literally spread all over the plate, meaning that not only was it not particularly effective for the duck (unless I was able to cut a chunk of strawberry/onion to accompany the bite), but that both the potatoes and the broccoli were swimming in it. Not an ideal pairing. A thicker sauce with more texture (e.g. more onion slivers) would have greatly improved the dish.

They showed me the dessert plate, but while the desserts looked good, it seemed like a bit more sugar than I wanted at that point, so I stopped there. All in all, this is a pleasant place. On food alone, it would probably be more like three and a half stars, but with the service and the pleasant atmosphere (other than the screaming baby, which they couldn't really control), I'll bump them to four stars and give them another try if I'm ever in the area again.

text:
GREAT food... My wife and I are huge BYOB fans and we track down anyone in the area that we haven't tried. So we i found that Spence312 moved into what use to be Avalon and i thought lets give it a shot. Apparently there was a Spence cafe at one point. (never tried it, wasnt from the area before) But who cares thats old news. This place is 5 stars all the way. Every course we had was amazing. 

My wife got She-Crab soup and it was blow your socks off good, we joked about asking for a bucket to go. I ordered the Flat bread special and was not let down at all. (i cant remember what all was on it, sounded fancy, tasted great sorry for the poor review on it but just order it)

For main course my wife got the Scallops which were very good. they had a cauliflower puree that i spend 5 mins telling my wife it was mashed potatoes and she promised me it was cauliflower. I said no one makes Caulifower this good.... it was Cauliflower, my wife was right.......again. I orderd the Lamb Shank (special that night) it was AMAZING... i have used that word too much in this review...lets go with it was DEVINE.... no lets just stick with AMAZING because it was. I hate every last bit and if the restraurant was empty i would have licked the plate clean!!!

Friendly service, it was a tuesday so it was quiet in the place. I am sure on a friday or saturday night it gets loud but that means your at a nice place, so deal with it, your there for the food not a quiet atmosphere. if thats what you want go to barnes and noble. Anyway Def give this shot a try, its got to be one of the best BYOB in West Chester!!!

After an afternoon of boating, Sea Dog Brewing Company hits the spot!

We came with friends who have a boat and were able to tie down right from the water, which is always nice and convenient.  The deck hands were super helpful and efficient, getting us tied and off the boat safely.

We were thirsty after spending time on the water so first thing we did was order drinks!  My husband and I ordered frozen Pain Killers, while our friends ordered a beer and a Mai Tai.  All of the drinks were perfectly made and tasted great!  Just what we needed to quench our thirst.

My husband shared the tuna appetizer and it was delicious.  The tuna was so fresh and the cucumbers and seaweed salad with it was perfect.  We also shared a burger (I can't remember which one), but it was really good and since I generally follow a low carb/keto diet, I ordered it without the bun, which was no problem for the kitchen.  

They have plenty of Sea Dog t-shirts, tank tops and koozies available in their retail area.  It's a popular place and both tourists and locals seem to patronize this restaurant and bar.

Our friends are regulars at Sea Dog since they have a condo in the area and are in town most weekends.  We would definitely go back again as the atmosphere is fun and the service and food were top notch as well.

Two words: RUM CAKE

We came in without reservations on New Years day and was able to get a table without a problem. I do recommend making reservations because it stayed pretty packed the entire time. Also, parking can be difficult. There are two hotels right before the restaurant, where you can pay to park. The restaurant is divided upstairs and downstairs, if you have a preference let them know. 

Appetizers:
Chilled Blue Crab Claws - Chili-basil vinaigrette
Grit Tots - Roasted red pepper coulis
Steamed Whitewater Mussels - Coconut-chili broth with fennel salad

Entrees:
Coriander Blackened Red Fish - Lump crab salad, honey cream mustard greens
Vegetable Curry - House made yellow curry, vadouvan roasted cauliflower, popcorn rice, garbanzos, goat peppers
Seared Sea Scallops - Roman artichokes, swiss chard, kalameta olive butter, grana pando

Desserts
Rum Glazed Pound Cake - Coconut semifreddo, caramelized pineapple, cayenne caramel (YASSSSSSS)
Tres Leche Bread Pudding  - Strawberry and candied pecans

Let me break it down.

Appetizers
The chilled blue crab claws were not properly cleaned, lots of shells. The flavors could have been more prominent or more of the chili-basil vinaigrette. The grit tots were pretty tasty! I wished for more cheese, but overall it paired perfectly with the roasted red pepper coulis! Now, the steamed whitewater mussels were a big miss for me. The "coconut-chili broth" made the entire dish hard to eat, very overpowering. The broth was more like a sweet coconut cream, rather than a light broth. If you can imagine what a dreamicle taste like... this was it. 

Entrees
Yay, finally some wins! Surprisingly, the vegetable curry was my favorite of all the entrees. The rice was perfectly cooked and the added goat peppers (tasted pickled) were a nice touch. I loved the bed of mustard greens and the acidic from the roasted tomatoes. The fish itself was a bit over cooked, but still a great balance of flavors. The scallops portions were huge! There were three perfectly tender scallops on a bed of swiss chard topped with artichokes. 

Desserts
What I would come back for? THIS RUM GLAZED POUND CAKE! I can't explain how much I'm in love with this dessert. The pound cake itself had a nice crispy crust with a buttery moist center. The sweet from the caramelized pineapple and spicy from the cayenne were my favor combos! Oh, and don't forget the delicious coconut semifreddo that pulls everything together. I'd say I didn't taste much "rum" from the dessert, but I loved it regardless. The tres leche bread pudding was okay. I felt that the bread pudding itself was a bit condensed and the pecans weren't caramelized.

Next time, 
I would try the Candied Fried Pork Ribs! Oh, and our service was A plus amazing! Our server did a great job at explaining each dish and making sure we were fully accommodated. I would have to say an exceptional job! Such a great place to experience the "New Orleans" culture.

Having read the reviews prior to coming here, I already expected bad service. But I was pleased with my first visit. I don't think the employees are rude or unfriendly, they're just trying to keep the line moving. So don't expect a happy greeting or having a social conversation about the weather with the employees. 

The side of Guacamole comes in Small or Large- except the large side is really a small and the small side is really an extra small. But for $3, it's not really that impressive. 

My torta came with beans but I asked for them on the side. When the cashier rung me up, he assumed the beans were an added on side and charged me an extra $1 without asking me first. When I saw the receipt I kindly explained to him the error but said it was fine, I just wanted him to know. I wasn't going to make a big deal over a dollar but felt he should know to double check first. By the time I got my drink and sat down, there was a dollar and change on my table. The worker returned the money he had overcharged me. 

I liked their little salsa bar and the different varieties they had. I really enjoyed their chips. This definitely makes sure your full before walking out. The Horchata was really good as well.

The food was really good. Idk if they're "street tacos" good, but definitely made me want to come back for me. I recommend this place!

First night in New Orleans, I was exhausted after the long drive into the city and an exciting Sugar Bowl Game at the Superdome.  I didn't get to eat in the stadium since I wanted to try some delicious food in New Orleans.  Unfortunately, by the time I got out of the game, it was very late and most places were closed.  After looking through Yelp, I found out that Crescent City Pizza Works was still open and open late.  I debated about this for a second since it was in the French Quarters and it was during a Bowl Game day, so I knew it was packed.  But, I had no other choice, so I decided to walk over and order a pizza to go. 

Once I got there, the line moved pretty quickly and I ordered a whole Pepperoni pizza to go.  It was also pretty decently prized.  The people who were working there were pretty nice.  Once I got the pizza, I started to head back to my hotel (I had my heart set on eating pizza in my room in my pajamas. LOL).  There is limited seating for those who want to eat there or pop in.  Since it was a super busy day, they blocked off most of French Quarter to traffic.  I just walked 2 blocks over and called an Uber.  It was pretty easy (aside from fending off some drunk people asking me if they can have a slice).  

As for the pizza, yum! I am not sure if it was extra good because I was so hungry.  But, the pizza crust was delicious and had the right amount of ingredients.  It was also cooked to perfection.  The one small complaint that I have is that the pizza was a little too greasy for me.  I ended up eating only about 1 slice (the slices were cut pretty big).  But, that's OK, I ended up having the other slices as snacks the next day.  I even ended up going back there in the next few days and ordered a few more slice (pepperoni was my favorite).  If you want a late night snack, I would definitely come here for your cravings.

I'm always excited to try a new restaurant, so we planned for a weekend lunch double date and had the chance to see a few of their signature dishes. This restaurant is new, so I anticipate they'll make some adjustments over time to get their stars up. I would return. 

To start, we ordered the shishito peppers, which are standard fare at any modern Asian restaurant, but the seasonings used at Red Bloom made something standard stand out. I would order this again. 

Next up: the pork belly bao buns. Definitely do yourself a favor and order these! The umami factor is not missed with this adventure of an appetizer. One in our party actually ordered them as her main.

For our entrees, we ordered two types of ramen, the pork belly and spicy miso. My ramen was not nearly as hot as it should have been, and the ramen noodles had been cooked too long. With ramen, you always serve the noodles al dente and allow the guest to determine the texture they want their noodles to be by serving it in the scalding hot liquid that the noodles sit and continue to cook in. Instead, that decision was made for me. Haru on Longley gets this concept right consistently, and having lived in Japan for two years, I appreciate their attention to authenticity.

The texture of all the ingredients in the bowl were also too similar, so this was an overall huge miss for me. The presentation was lazy for a dish you can enjoy for less at Haru. Take a look at my ramen from there and ask yourself which one is worth $18.

The spicy miso, which comes with a warning of two chiles on the menu, is not spicy -- not even a little bit.

The friendliness and warmth of our server, Angelo, was very inviting.

Although nobody in our party was Asian, I do have to make mention of the fact that this restaurant was designed and decorated using quite a lot of white. White is a color associated with purity, but it's also a color associated with death and mourning and is reminiscent of funerals. I don't know why Americans insist on upscale Asian concepts being so white.

No superstitious Hong Kong high roller is going to want to start their gambling evening with a meal in a restaurant with so much white; it's considered very unlucky.

You might drive past this place 100 times and not even realize it's here. Off of Kietzke Ln in an old strip mall. 

But if you're ever in the mood for a shake, burger or hotdog, this is your place. 

The lady who works the cash register on Saturdays, is really nice and works really hard. 

I like getting a cheese burger usually. And my kids like the cheeseburgers here too, and oddly enough, the tacos are yummy. We also share orders of onion rings, French fries, or chips with cheese. 

It's always clean. And the space is pretty big, so there are plenty of tables when it's busy. 

Definitely recommend!

Cheap quality food, tacky environment, chipped China all round, spoiled water. Not worth the price they ask for.

I order a chocolate soufflé, however, it collapsed it the kitchen. The chef ended up serving me chocolate mousse. He had the nerve to tell me that chocolate mousse is the same as chocolate soufflé but served cold. What kind of "5 star- top chef" tell this to his customers assuming that they don't know anything about food?!?

Hooray for Banh Mi for $3.25.  For that much, I'm willing to put up with a lot of crap but I'd say this is as good as Banh Mi So's... or maybe it's the convenient location that's making me like it more...

Regardless, the Lady likes Kim Son more so we don't come here anywhere near as often as I'd like, but I'd still like to point out that this place is quite different from a lot of the other Vietnamese places in town and the city that would make it worth the trek to check out.  

I still like the crispy squid a lot as well as their grilled beef (pretty much any of their dishes involved grilled beef.)  But those cheap delicious sammiches will definitely be the thing I'll get the most from there.

It will be even more convenient to get to when they move by the metrolink by 170 and Eager...

Like eating in your old Cambodian grandmother's living room, if you had an old Cambodian grandmother, and if my imagination serves me right. 

I don't have a Cambodian grandmother, however, so new Phnom Penh will do! 

Had their namesake noodle soup with some fried youtiaw (Chinese cruller) and the spring rolls. 

Quite good. Quite homey. Not watered down for American taste at all. And that is appreciated. 

Clean broth with good flavor to start. Meats in the soup are as traditional as they come. Heart, liver, Cambodian pork roll/sausage, maybe kidney, and such...a little ground pork...rice noodles, scallions and a bit of pickled greens. A side of sprouts and lime, and yummy chili vinegar, chili paste, and sambal and it hit the spot. 

Spring rolls rolled with rice paper and fried. Crunchy , and a hint of funk in a good way. Nice fishy dipping sauce accompanied. 

One tip, as i observed everyone else eating there doing so, order the noodle soup "dry" with the broth on the side. Looked good that way. 

Definitely need to try the bo kho next time too.

Will certainly be back.

The poor rating is for treatment of the staff.  With first hand experience I can tell you we had to fight with Peter for our daughter to be compensated for the shifts she worked. He wanted to dock her two shifts to pay for the Nitza's T-shirt. His wife was pleading for him to pay she was clearly uncomfortable trying to bridge our expectations and her husbands refusal.  Our persistence paid off eventually. His use of profanity directed at these kids is unacceptable.   Being a customer previously I had only seen a wonderful side of Peter. Kind, happy and engaging. Be warned as we know our experience is not isolated.

First I want to say this was a very friendly restaurant I was greeted as soon as I walked in and he asked if I had been in before. Which I hadn't . I ordered drunken noodle . As soon as it came out i saw how they didn't prepare it in the usual way, which is fine trying a new prepared dish is good . I took one bite and knew I wasn't going to get through it they had put sooo much soy sauce in it it tasted like a salt lick . Such a bummer since I love Thai food so much . In the back of my head I thought well it is a Chinese / Thai  restaurant . I am biased because I don't care for Chinese food but It was closest to my hotel. I would definitely not recommend it if you are a Thai food fan. They need to stick to Chinese since it had more of a Chinese flair. And change their drunken noodle recipe .. terrible ... but I would recommend the Chinese dishes the ones I saw coming out looked great !

Extremely unsanitary! After experiencing the cashier take my order, sweep, take another order, take my second order, sweep and then place a bratwurst, two burgers, and fries into their appropriate cooking stations, I made a recommendation to a second line cook, "to see if it was possible for the cook to wash her hands prior to going back to cooking" 

The second individual, cocked her eyes wide open and stated, "the grill is extremely that's not a problem", and then walked away from the counter and began to share with the third cook, who at the time was cleaning the area's stainless. 

As a customer, who has worked in two fast food environments throughout my undergrad experience, if I know anything other than my Masters of Social Work background from Washington University, I KNOW sanitary and cleanliness....as well as customer service! 

I experienced the line cooks look to me as if I had horribly discussed their mother, threw ketchup on their hands, ran my debit card through 10 times...all to continuously receive the "declined" notification! 

I offered a suggestion, not a request for a refund. Yet, I received the WORST backlash ever. This was between the hours of 8-9:30pm on a Tuesday night! 

I sat at my table (to enjoy my mom's bday), and shortly after settled with knowing that my experience was not worth the "cheap food, 1/2lb cheeseburger for $2.60 tax included". 

I asked my husband for our receipt, explained my experience, and had the go ahead to ask for a refund. 

As I walked over to the counter, the woman who I expressed my concern/suggestion to was speaking with the manager. I approached the manger, and before I could begin to speak, he extended his hand towards my receipt. I followed up by asking him if he was already aware of the situation and he noted yes, signed the receipt and handed it over to the woman I had spoken to. She walked to the register, made the transaction, returned my funds, and walked away. 

In a complete awe, I silently walked over to my table and could not help wanting to share! However, I did not want to ruin the experience of the individual's at my table. So YELP has turned into my outlet. 

Ultimately, it's such a downer as a customer, a respectful and paying customer.....to negatively experience 3 line cooks ....and then the shift's or maybe the store manager. Surprisingly, they were all over the age of 30. Two were certainly over 40. 

How about a 35 minute drive to engage in poor customer service AND poor sanitation practices. No one utilized gloves, regardless of their ability to simultaneously cook, clean stainless, sweep, and scrap their grills.

Even after the burgers were cooked, I saw the ladies finishing all of their food preparations without gloves. 

I would like to end by sharing that the waiters....were AMAZING! Very kind, explanatory, and lots of smiles. Certainly did not impose any abrasive attitude upon me!

This place has completely won my heart over. 

In a nutshell, the Malvern Buttery is clean, ethical, reasonably priced food paired with a simple but elegant coffee bar in a gorgeous and yet also very kid friendly setting. 

I was a bit thrown for a loop by the unique buffet style of service, but it works and after my second visit I now find it endearing. The food is all very good and the barista definitely knew what she was doing. 

I sat at a sunny table, sipped on my latte and worked on my laptop for close to two hours and could have stayed longer. It's a great place to grab a quick bite to eat or a coffee to go - but I'd recommend sticking around. 

What a gift this place is to Malvern!

I found out why this place has such good reviews.  Divey little restaurant on a hip street, where I had probably the best vegetable biryani I've ever eaten.  And a pretty good Turkish coffee.  Friendly, personable service.  With a pretty generous tip, my total came to $20.

Try the masala sauce on the side....no matter what you order. :)

Yeah, not feeling the love for this establishment.  I've been to IHOPs all over Nashville and out of town. This location by far has THE SLOWEST service ever! The waitress was nice and friendly.  She smiled and provided correct orders but there was no apology or urgency in her stewardship. My visit was on a Saturday morning, understandably peak hours. We were seated quickly but there was no hello from the waitress until maybe 10 - 20 minutes later.  The sad part is she was serving the table right next to us and never said a mumbling word until she was completely done serving them check and all. She came to their table at least twice if not 3 times and within those visits never said hello, I'll be right with you or anything until she delivered their check and they left.  If I hadn't had my godson and dropped $2 in the meter I surely would have packed up and moved on. 
Once we were finally offered to place our order the food took another 20 minutes or so.  IHOPs all over the world are busy on the weekends. This is the first time I've had such a lengthy wait for my order. From the looks of it my waitress had one other table. They were there before me and from how they were chit chatting it seemed they had already finished their meal. No.  They had an extensive wait as well. All I could do was shake my head. 
Needless to say, I won't be back to this location.

In the last month, I have eaten more chicago style pizzas than I have my whole life (which until a month ago was zero!)

My sister and brother in law had been raving about this place, we absolutely must try it.  We arrived as they open, as insiders know the place gets PACKED.  It's in an old converted house, with wooden booths in different rooms, trivial pursuit cards at the table.  Since my hubs is typically non pork eating and I'm non veggies on my pizza eating, we had to make it difficult with halving the pizzas - which turned out to not be difficult at all, even with a curve ball thrown at our server.  We got the deep dish, half cappy, half something without veggies and we got a new york style, half cappy, half non pork.  

Would you believe that the 4 of us ate almost ALL of it?! (A med and large).  It was super super delicious.  Ambiance, price, food, location....I'll definitely be back!

I've never been to a bike shop that is also a coffee shop, but me gusto! It's also pet friendly (they have dog treats at the register!). 

The staff is always friendly and greet me with a warm smile and hello. They move quickly and they make a meannnnnn dirty chai! 

There are lots of outdoor seating, a high work bench in front of the window, and a long table in the middle of the shop. It has never been too crowded, so seating and spacing isn't an issue.

They also sell really cool looking bike gear. I think they repair bikes on the left side of the shop. 

Totally a hip spot to get coffee in the CBD.

I'm surprised there is only one review for this place.  I guess Yelpers don't get down to the South County strip malls very often.   The wife and I enjoyed lunch at Lemay Wok the other day.   The price is just under $7 for most dishes.  We had gotten carry-out a couple of times before and found the food to be just okay, but with the top rating given by the Riverfrnot Times, we thought we'd give it another try.  

The place was packed, which we found surprising on a Saturday afternoon.   We had Pork Egg Foo Yung and Chicken and Broccoli (spicy, by request).  Fried rice comes normally, but we just got white rice in a weak attempt to eat healthy.  Both dishes were very good and the egg drop soup that came first was also excellent.  

We'll probably go back and try something more exotic someday, since they did such a good job on these very ordinary items.  I wouldn't describe Lemay Wok as a destination restaurant based on our limited experience, but if you like "American Style" Chinese,  and you live in South County, give it a try.   

I'll update if/when we try something more interesting here.

Ok, a raised carnivore visiting a vegan restaurant? Yeah, hell has officially frozen over. But this place is absolutely amazing and I will tell you why.
I always wanted to try a vegan meal. So I came to this place. It was the picture of the tart that drew me in. Yes, the dessert was the deal breaker. 
My father died when I was 17 of coronary heart disease. My mom has type 2 diabetes and I wanted to change my lifestyle. 
They have a lot of different options and I walked in so utterly confused on what to choose. The lady at the register was so helpful.
So I ended up having a Mac and cheese platter. The dish was very flavorful and did not have a lot of peas. The dish also had tempeh which tasted a lot like bacon. I asked one of the cooks that this couldn't be a vegan dish because of the bacon taste. He laughed and confirmed that it was 100 percent vegan. 
For dessert I had one of their tarts, which looked like a peanut butter chocolate tart, but actually had a coconut nutty blend to it. It wasn't too sweet and it didn't feel like I had a huge lump in my stomach. 
The people again were very friendly and gave me a ton of information on how to switch from a carnivore/omnivore diet to a vegetarian/vegan diet.
This place also has free yoga sessions that ask for donations. 
The food is a bit expensive, but with the good customer service, I think I will be back.

I dined here with a group of 5 other friends this evening and it was a hit and miss experience. The good: The service. Our server was knowledgeable, would find out what she didn't know, and was attentive. Our table was always clear, we were never lacking for water or any other beverage. The restaurant was described to us as a shared plate concept-- which we were familiar with-- and we ordered a few small plates, a large plate and a steak to share. The desserts were also a highlight-- we really liked the Cheesecake beignets. 

The bad: The food all came out at the same time. I'm a big fan of eating food when it's hot and in it's most perfect state-- everything except the steak came out at the same time (and we had to ask that they hold the steak or it would have sat on the table forever). Speaking of our steak-- it was lacking serious flavor. It was cooked to our liking (medium rare) but the flavor just wasn't there. They offer all sorts of sauce accouterment but IMO steak shouldn't need a buttery sauce. 

The OK: The remainder of our dishes were good. Not great, not bad-- just good. Peoples favorites seemed to be the Foraged Mushrooms and the Crispy Duck. Much everything else was unremarkable. 

I'm in Nashville every few months and love trying new places-- I also love to eat food that feels inspired-- my guess is that I won't return as there are so many really amazing restaurants in town now. 

Tidbits: Valet is $3, lighting is nice, design is clean and sophisticated-- but approachable, and the location is great.

I'd like to clear up some misconceptions that I had before coming here from the Yelp reviews:
-They do take credit cards
-There is plenty of seating inside.  In fact it looks like a breeding ground for chairs and tables
-I had no problem parking

Now that that's out of the way....we had a small tomato pie (which has cheese on it, just under the sauce) and a buffalo chicken panini.  Both were delicious.  The pie had a sweet sauce and we got in on whole wheat crust, which made me feel better and it tasted fine.  

My biggest highlight was the owner.  He was talkative and clearly cares.  The Casey Anthony verdict had just dropped and he was yelling at Nancy Grace on the TV.  That's when I knew I liked him, for the enemy of my enemy is my friend.

I wanted something different for lunch today. Tired of the same ole' sonic, taco bell, burgerking fix. Was looking for restaurants in Lavergne and read about the Noodle House. I will admit I was hesitate to go into the locale, but once inside the A-frame building it's completely relaxed. 

I ordered the Panang Chicken with Sticky Rice ( I cant believe they actually had sticky rice!! So many people claim to have real Thai/Loas dishes but no sticky rice) 

It hit the spot! I would definitely recommend and I am definitely going back!

Brunch for less than $10?! What???

I was initially a little confused about what this place was -- is it a clothing store? Is it a coffee shop? Is it a brunch place? I'm pretty sure it's all 3. 

The drinks are a little pricier than similar coffee shops, but the food is surprisingly cheap. I had a filling and delicious plate of grit cakes with 2 eggs and sausage for $7.85! The rest of the menu seems pretty simple and fairly health conscious, which I appreciate. Most of the breakfast menu is less than $10. 

The mission of the place seems to be very environmentally friendly, which is always nice. The interior is very cool and cafe area is made to look like a cabin. Even if you don't need to use the restroom, I suggest you go anyway because it's super cool!

Worst store EVER!!! This store price-gouges their items to the point where I  feel the Attorney General & D.A. need to step-in... Not only are the food & non-food items ridiculously overpriced, I've got a handful of friends who have ALL gotten food poisoning from the food items that are prepared on site. 
AVOID THIS PLACE LIKE THE PLAGUE!!! 
FYI: I've live in this neighborhood for 2.5 yrs. in case you care to know. 
Thank JEEBUS I own a vehicle so I can shop at Save-a-Lot & Ideal Market #2... these are the best places to shop for value & cheap prices... especially if you boycott Walmart ;-)

Quality food and ingredients. Hope this place becomes as popular as their Mayberry Location. I love that Wells Ave. is coming alive! Great service, great coffee, great food. Even the teenager approved!

No soap in the women's bathroom. A female employee came in there after me & walked out drying her wet hands on her pants. We didn't eat here. This review is based solely on that cleanliness/ hygiene on May 29, 2021.

Went here with some friends.  It's a casual place where you order at the counter and they will bring your order to you.  They have strombolis, pasta, and sandwiches as well as the pizza.   For the pizza you start with a cheese pizza and have your choice of ingredients to add on.  Some are 75 cents a piece and premium toppings are twice as much.  You can get pizza by the slice and the slice is very large and filling.  It had a lot of fluid on top which I patted off with napkins.  It is a pizza you can fold over New York style.  I thought it tasted good.  Prices are very reasonable.  I would go back again.

Visited this bar a few weeks ago and had lunch with my husband and friend. A lunch on Saturday took 40 minutes to receive. They were extremely slow and the server wasn't too concerned. Food was good though so we brushed it off as a bad day. My husband and I tried to visit tonight waited 10 minutes and were never greeted or acknowledged. The couple sitting next to us had to fetch their check from inside. Just a weird vibe from this place in general if you want good service go elsewhere.

We always enjoy coming here to have drinks and dinner. The Smokey Old Fashion that they make here is always amazing and affordable enough where you can have 2, which is more than enough on a week night. The hosts and servers are always real nice and down to earth (especially for a very hipster type place). I haven't ordered something I haven't liked yet. The truffle parmesan fries are always a must have. The past time we had the flatbread which was great. The artesian bread made the flatbread that much better. We also got the burger and Caesar salad which was grilled (my favorite). This place is always great because of the ambiance, people, drinks and food. A new thing I learned, they mostly feature local ingredients and local crafts. Love supporting local businesses.

Organic, Seasonal, Sustainable, Local Ingredients. To most of my friends that doesn't mean much, but to me it means that the people at Jules care about both their product, their customers and the world around them. I do go back here for my regular pizza fix, because it is the best game in town. From their Pepperoni to their Chicken, Gorgonzola and Caramelized onion, to the frisee and goat cheese salads and homemade dressings, everything is delicious.

Came here with a few friends and we were put into the backroom where it was almost like a quarantine chamber. The service was very slow and our server rude and unhelpful. He decided on his own to put everyone on one bill and when we asked for a bill split he said he can't do it. He messed up our order and receipt like 4 times. None of us will ever come back here. I've been to many bars and restaurants never have I heard a bill can't be split.

There should be a zero star option, or after tonight's experience, negative stars. 

My boyfriend and I used to come here at least once a week....that is until tonight. I ordered my usual quesadilla rellena. Half way through my meal, my boyfriend discovers not 1, but THREE dirty fingernails on my tomatoes and rice. 

THREE. DIRTY. FINGERNAILS!!!!!!!!!!! That is not apart of my special!

We presented this to the waiter and the waiter responded with "eh.okay. I'll bring you your check" which proceeds with a long wait.

Unless you want fingernail clippings in your food, go somewhere else. Mexican food will now consist of driving out of the vue to go to Sopapillas, where I have yet to discover fingernail clippings.

Freaking. disgusting.
Employees are always friendly and service is always as fast as you'd expect. Our order has always been correct. Overall, this location is a safe bet for lunch or dinner.
